webpage.text:
MPs Furious Over 'Shambolic' European Vote | Politics News

The Government has been denounced in furious scenes in Parliament and accused of trying to renege on a controversial vote on the European Arrest Warrant.

Amid claims of "chaos, shambles and chicanery", Commons Speaker John Bercow said MPs had been irritated by the Government's handling of the issue and that the public would be "contemptuous".

Britain will continue to be a member of the European Arrest Warrant system. However, there has been no specific vote on its inclusion in a raft of 35 measures from the EU covering criminal justice and policing.

Early on Monday evening, Mr Bercow confirmed only 11 of these measures were going to be discussed, with the controversial European Arrest Warrant not one of them.

This prompted wide-ranging criticism from MPs, with one Eurosceptic describing the Government's move as "completely unacceptable" and a "disgraceful way of going about a very, very important matter".

Commons Chaos Could Cost The Tories

Sky News Political Editor Faisal Islam said: "There was a clear attempt to slightly muddy the waters for Parliament in order to minimise the potential Conservative rebellion. But that was achieved through slightly underhand means which were then called out by Parliament.

"The boil of the European Arrest Warrant issue within the Conservative Party is far from lanced. They have picked at a wound and might have infected it ahead of this crucial Rochester and Strood by-election, and UKIP are smiling tonight."

Shadow home secretary Yvette Cooper described the scenes in Parliament as "complete chaos" and a "shambles".

She said: "Labour proposed to the Government to have a vote on the European Arrest Warrant and the remaining EU measures tomorrow, which there is time for and which we would support.

"It was within the Government's power to put right the chaos and deception they have created, but they chose not to do so.

"The House of Commons should be able to vote to endorse the European Arrest Warrant, putting it beyond legal challenge - which we know Eurosceptics have been planning.

"Despite being promised this vote, the Commons has been denied the chance to give overwhelming backing to this crucial crimefighting measure. The Government must put that right at the earliest opportunity.

"Theresa May was very foolish not to listen to the strong support across the House both for the European Arrest Warrant and for the opportunity of a comprehensive vote. She has handled this dreadfully. It's a complete mess." 

Supporters of the warrant insist that it ensures that suspects of crime in Britain are quickly returned if they flee to an EU member state.

However, critics warn it could cause UK citizens, wanted on minor charges, to be flown to a country where there is no guarantee of a fair trial.

brut.title: Youth Parliament takes over Commons - BBC News

webpage.text:
Youth Parliament takes over Commons

On the living wage, Caitlin Smith said: "I have a Saturday job I work on Saturday afternoons and my hourly pay is £3.79.

"That means that my dad pays more in petrol to drive me to that job than I actually earn… we have a democratic mandate to support this issue."

Monica Yianni, gave a speech in rhyming verse, saying "we need a new Magna Carta, you can call it what you will.

"No living creature no matter where, should have to foot the bill.

"It doesn't matter who you are, nor where you are from, nor your gender, your race your religion. We all just need to get along."

In his closing speech, Minhaz Abedin said: "I was going to start this speech with we made it, but then I realised it was a bit better than that, 969,992 young people made it.

"Every person in this chamber has witnessed something historic today, so let us take a second to realise what we have actually accomplished.
